Tolerance / SLOs:

- Streaming is required (we rely on partial tokens for UI responsiveness) - ideally token flush every 150-200ms.

Hi Alex - Sean here (solutions eng). Quick technical answers and an initial recommendation.

Warm pool vs reactive scaling:
- We support both. For your profile I recommend a hybrid: a small warm pool sized to handle the first 30-40% of expected burst (e.g., 800 workers) plus reactive scaling to fill remaining capacity.
- Typical scale-up time (cold -> ready) depends on deployment mode: hosted API cold-starts ~60-90s to get new GPU workers fully warmed (model weights + KV cache priming). Dedicated + reserved warm pool can reduce effective time to <10s for pre-warmed instances.

Queueing & backpressure:
- By default we use a prioritized queue: interactive streaming requests get higher priority; background/batch jobs are deprioritized. Queueing is FIFO within priority buckets.
- We implement token-level backpressure and early flush heuristics so streaming responses can provide partial results while upstream requests wait in queue.
- Circuit-breaker behavior: when queue depth for high-priority bucket exceeds threshold, we can (configurable) 1) shed low-priority traffic, 2) enforce per-tenant rate limits, or 3) return quick fallback responses (e.g., condensed summary) to preserve p95 for interactive flows.

Autoscaling recommendations (initial):
- Warm pool: reserve 800 pre-warmed workers (covers ~30-40% of 2500 spike).
- Reactive policy: aggressive ramp for first 90s (aim to provision additional workers in 60-90s), then sustained autoscale to handle remaining load within 3-5 minutes.
- Queue policy: priority buckets with 30s soft queue for medium priority; 0-5s target queue for interactive token streams.
- Canary gating: route 5-10% of traffic to canary scale profile during PoC to monitor regressions.

Cost notes:
- Warm pool has a steady cost; Dedicated reserved pools (monthly commit) provide best unit economics for predictable bursts. Hosted on-demand with aggressive reactive scaling may increase per-token cost during frequent spikes. We’ll quantify in the MAP.

Attachment: autoscale-config-suggestion.yml (sample config for warm pool + reactive policies). I’ll follow up with an expanded cost estimate and test plan.
